prompt_text:
You are extending one independently audited open-problem draft in a sealed paired experiment.

Read only source /evidence/source.json, parent /evidence/parent.json, and independent audit /evidence/audit.json. Do not use the web, any prior-run file other than those exact sealed inputs, any other solution, or any verification report. You may create exact-arithmetic checks only under /work; do not modify files outside /work.

Parent SHA-256: ac8e93706ae8e7a430b0e804ec300545326370f2ee32584573ee72dded925651
Audit SHA-256: 8da73b573b2f6140568cfc36430783cd02f2f6ef5ed1e7d2b8653954cd608c57

This is an exact-closure attempt after the three scheduled search lenses. Concentrate on resolving the independent audit. If no material proof change is required, copy claimed_resolution, every claim and proof_sketch, and final_writeup from the parent exactly.

Address every REFUTED or UNRESOLVED claim and the audit's target-coverage judgment. Preserve correct progress. Repair, narrow, replace, or remove unsupported claims. Never call the open target solved without a complete proof at the requested strength. Put every load-bearing claim in a separate results item in proof order. There is no claim-count cap. The entire ordered proof is in scope. Keep final_writeup under 3,000 words and each proof_sketch under 500 words.

Complete independent audit:
--- BEGIN AUDIT ---
{
  "record_id": "tcs_h3_free_induced_disjoint_paths",
  "stage": "REVISION_AUDIT",
  "arm": "plain",
  "iteration": 4,
  "parent_sha256": "ac8e93706ae8e7a430b0e804ec300545326370f2ee32584573ee72dded925651",
  "complete": true,
  "claims": [
    {
      "idx": 0,
      "claim": "The fixed-k problems are monotone under padding: k-Induced Disjoint Paths reduces to ℓ-Induced Disjoint Paths for every fixed ℓ≥k while preserving H3-freeness. Moreover, k=1 is linear-time solvable and every fixed-k problem is in NP.",
      "claim_sha256": "bb4de64fb53864bbf8f528badde7a0d768aa737b3eefc4564e93b3ecafa24a75",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Adding ℓ−k disjoint K2 components with their endpoints as new terminal pairs is an equivalence-preserving polynomial reduction. Since H3 is connected and has eight vertices, the union is H3-free exactly when the original graph is. For k=1, connectivity is necessary and sufficient and can be tested by BFS/DFS; a shortest connecting path is induced. For fixed k, the paths form a polynomial-size certificate whose endpoints, disjointness, and cross-path nonadjacency are directly checkable.",
      "witness": "The padding instance is G disjoint-union (ℓ−k)K2; restriction and extension of linkages are inverse operations.",
      "search_method": "Direct proof from the source definitions; no external search.",
      "checker_path": "none"
    },
    {
      "idx": 1,
      "claim": "Every H3-free graph is 6-degenerate, with the constant sharp; additionally, two vertices of degree at least three can never be at distance exactly three. Thus an n-vertex H3-free graph has at most 6n−21 edges for n≥7, and every connected H3-free graph of minimum degree at least three has diameter at most two.",
      "claim_sha256": "d498bb9e6250b3ca55905f675549c6f5eeb6cc7d6c947badc7c5c75e7dcf09e2",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "For a geodesic u-x-y-v, two additional neighbors of u and two of v are outside the geodesic and pairwise distinct across the two sides; otherwise u and v would be closer than three. Those eight vertices and the required edges form H3 as a subgraph. A graph of minimum degree at least seven contains every eight-vertex tree by greedy parent-first embedding, so every subgraph of an H3-free graph has a vertex of degree at most six. Summing backward degrees in a degeneracy order gives 6n−21 for n≥7. The distance result applied to a length-three subpath of a geodesic gives the diameter conclusion.",
      "witness": "K7 is H3-free because it has only seven vertices and has degeneracy six, proving sharpness.",
      "search_method": "Direct extremal and geodesic arguments from the definition of H3.",
      "checker_path": "none"
    },
    {
      "idx": 2,
      "claim": "H3-free graphs admit an arbitrary-routing-plus-matching normal form. Let R be any graph and M a matching on V(R), disjoint from E(R). Replace every edge of R by a four-edge path and retain every edge of M unsubdivided, obtaining G(R,M). Then G(R,M) is H3-free. With all terminals in V(R), induced linkages in G(R,M) correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M such that every M-edge whose two endpoints are selected is itself used between consecutive vertices of one path. In particular, the H3-free class has unbounded treewidth.",
      "claim_sha256": "690ebb3806af1ca6f9ca316c27fe6e0db1a4548a2a1ae6714ff324c5c8e8e165",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "Subdivision vertices have degree two, so H3 centers would both have to be original vertices. A three-edge path starting through an R-corridor cannot reach another original vertex, while one starting with an M-edge has only two remaining steps and cannot use another M-edge because M is a matching. Hence H3 cannot occur. Paths with original endpoints traverse each used corridor completely. Contracting corridors therefore gives vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M, and the only possible extra selected-vertex adjacencies are M-edges, yielding exactly the stated matching-clean condition. Conversely, lifting a matching-clean family introduces no chords or cross-path edges.",
      "witness": "With M empty and R=K_m, G(R,M) contains K_m as a minor, so its treewidth is at least m−1. The exact checker also found no H3 in all tested labelled R,M constructions on at most five original vertices for corridor lengths four and five.",
      "search_method": "Bidirectional structural proof plus exhaustive finite corroboration.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_h3_free_induced_disjoint_paths/audit/plain/attempt_4/h3_audit_exact_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 3,
      "claim": "Conditional contraction lemma: if R and M are supplied, M is a matching on V(R) disjoint from E(R), G=G(R,M), and all terminals are distinct vertices of V(R), then preprocessing matching edges with two terminal endpoints and contracting every remaining edge of M reduces induced linkage in G exactly to ordinary vertex-disjoint linkage in a quotient graph. Consequently, for every fixed k this represented-input, original-terminal problem is polynomial-time solvable.",
      "claim_sha256": "76d60e1f65901a1fba6c4ec563fe94d0b1db7fd3d5865f30074aeda868736204",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "A matching edge joining terminals of different pairs makes a solution impossible; one equal to a prescribed pair can be fixed and removed. Every remaining matching edge has at most one terminal. A matching-clean linkage contracts to vertex-disjoint quotient paths. Conversely, at each visited matched class, the two incident route edges determine whether the lift uses one endpoint or crosses the matching edge; a terminal class is lifted starting at its actual terminal. Disjoint quotient paths use disjoint matching classes, so the lift is vertex-disjoint and matching-clean. Four-subdividing the quotient converts ordinary linkage to induced linkage on an H1-subgraph-free graph, for which the sealed source states fixed-k polynomial solvability.",
      "witness": "The checker exhaustively compared matching-clean linkage with the contracted ordinary-linkage instance for 10,288 labelled represented instances on four or five original vertices, including both kinds of terminal-terminal matching edge, with no discrepancy.",
      "search_method": "Proof of both contraction directions, terminal-case analysis, and exhaustive exact enumeration.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_h3_free_induced_disjoint_paths/audit/plain/attempt_4/h3_audit_exact_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 4,
      "claim": "The conditional contraction lemma does not establish polynomial-time solvability for standard instances on the entire graph class {G(R,M)}: a standard instance supplies only G, may put terminals at subdivision vertices, and need not determine a unique R,M representation. Therefore the classification for every fixed k≥2 remains open in this draft.",
      "claim_sha256": "e06a789cbb2f89664cfab1876ca2b9fb5cdcba2c22fa0c8eae1c9373dad3c802",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "The lemma explicitly assumes supplied R,M and original-vertex terminals, neither of which is part of a standard promised-class instance. None of the other draft results supplies representation recovery, handles arbitrary subdivision terminals, gives a full-class algorithm, or proves hardness for a fixed k≥2. Thus the limitation and the draft-level nonclassification follow.",
      "witness": "A four-edge K2 corridor permits internal subdivision terminals outside V(R). The labelled P6 has one representation using 0-1-2-3-4 as an R-corridor and 4-5 as M, and another using 0-1 as M and 1-2-3-4-5 as an R-corridor.",
      "search_method": "Input-model comparison and direct verification of the two explicit path representations.",
      "checker_path": "none"
    },
    {
      "idx": 5,
      "claim": "Four is the sharp universal corridor length in the arbitrary-routing-plus-matching construction: replacing every R-edge by a path of any fixed length d≥4 always produces an H3-free graph after retaining M, whereas each d∈{1,2,3} has a permitted pair (R,M) whose resulting graph contains H3.",
      "claim_sha256": "3b4be52685ed8d2fe1d293bdedf7fc14bbc85a85bc031d384b5fc527eb4c8133",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "For d≥4, the degree argument from claim 2 excludes a three-edge path between possible centers: after entering an R-corridor the path cannot reach an original vertex, and after an initial M-edge the remaining two steps also cannot do so. The proposed constructions for d=1,2,3 each contain the required center path and four distinct leaves.",
      "witness": "For d=1 use R=H3, M empty. For d=3 use R=K4, M empty. For d=2 use R-edges up, uq, vw, wr, ws and M-edge uv; if a subdivides vw, u-v-a-w is the H3 center path.",
      "search_method": "Universal degree/path proof and exact checking of all three sharpness witnesses.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_h3_free_induced_disjoint_paths/audit/plain/attempt_4/h3_audit_exact_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 6,
      "claim": "For arbitrary graphs, hence also for H3-free graphs, k-Induced Disjoint Paths is fixed-parameter tractable in k+b, where b is the number of vertices of degree at least three. There is an exact equivalent compression with at most b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices.",
      "claim_sha256": "572f4e3b7c94a2ec34f966014a296adb2229a1c2e623bf55ed18f979ec7acc89",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "After deleting the b branching vertices, every component is a path, isolated vertex, or unattached cycle and has at most two attachments. A terminal-free component is usable only as a corridor between two distinct branching vertices, so one two-edge representative per unordered pair suffices. In a terminal-bearing component, every unmarked gap between terminals and attachment occurrences is either unused or traversed completely; retaining one-edge gaps and replacing each longer gap by a two-edge path preserves endpoint adjacency and permits exact lifting. There are at most 2k terminal vertices, binom(b,2) generic representatives, and at most 4k gap representatives, giving the stated bound. Exhaustive solution enumeration on the compressed graph is a function only of k+b, with polynomial preprocessing and lifting.",
      "witness": "The checker constructed the compression and compared feasibility on every labelled graph with four fixed terminals and four, five, or six vertices—33,856 graphs total—with no discrepancy; it also checked the claimed size bound in every case.",
      "search_method": "Degree-two component decomposition, explicit collapse/lift proof, counting, and exhaustive exact enumeration.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_h3_free_induced_disjoint_paths/audit/plain/attempt_4/h3_audit_exact_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 7,
      "claim": "A globally shortest path for one terminal pair cannot be fixed greedily, even on a seven-vertex H3-free graph.",
      "claim_sha256": "cbbd8530f9b2f64cffec987b3e5d6400cf0331fe452a232ae8a252828e8c9559",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "The displayed graph has fewer than the eight vertices required for H3. The paths s1-y-z-t1 and s2-t2 are mutually induced. The only length-two s1-t1 path is s1-x-t1, while every alternative is longer; its edge xs2 conflicts with the forced s2-t2 path. Thus the unique global shortest path cannot be part of a solution although the instance is positive.",
      "witness": "Vertices s1,t1,x,s2,t2,y,z and edges s1x, xt1, xs2, s2t2, s1y, yz, zt1.",
      "search_method": "Direct path enumeration and independent exact checker.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_h3_free_induced_disjoint_paths/audit/plain/attempt_4/h3_audit_exact_checker.py"
    },
    {
      "idx": 8,
      "claim": "The seven-vertex obstruction is vertex-minimal for the unique-shortest formulation and also defeats total-length minimization: no graph on at most six vertices with four distinct terminals has an induced linkage while the first pair's unique globally shortest path is unextendable, and in the seven-vertex witness the unique minimum-total-length ordinary two-linkage is not induced.",
      "claim_sha256": "ba5fed6558a3eb55a2c9b79d15a5a17a4ab23c982ff8ccb3a3ad197b2d956ea3",
      "verdict": "VERIFIED",
      "evidence": "If P1,P2 are a solution but the unique shortest first-pair path Q is unextendable, then Q is strictly shorter than P1. P1 must have at least three edges: if it had two, the only shorter option would be the terminal edge, which remains compatible with P2. On at most six vertices this forces P1 to use four vertices and P2 to be the terminal edge using the other two. Q then has two edges. Its internal vertex either lies in P1, making Q compatible with P2, or lies in P2, making its two incident edges forbidden cross-path edges—both contradictions. In the seven-vertex graph, s2t2 is the only second-pair path and s1-x-t1 is the unique shortest first-pair path, so their union uniquely minimizes total length but is not induced because of xs2.",
      "witness": "Exact enumeration found no obstruction among all 33,856 labelled graphs on four through six vertices with terminals fixed by symmetry, and confirmed the unique non-induced total-length minimizer in the stated seven-vertex graph.",
      "search_method": "Vertex-count proof plus exhaustive exact enumeration of all graphs through six vertices and all relevant paths.",
      "checker_path": "<workspace-home>/paired_v2_fixed_point_extension_v3_scratch/tcs_h3_free_induced_disjoint_paths/audit/plain/attempt_4/h3_audit_exact_checker.py"
    }
  ],
  "confirmed_refutations": [],
  "target_verdict": "VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS",
  "claimed_resolution_verdict": "ACCURATE",
  "target_evidence": "The source target asks for a complexity classification for every fixed k on all H3-subgraph-free graphs. The draft correctly settles k=1 and proves several structural and parameterized results, including a polynomial algorithm only for the narrower represented-input/original-terminal model. It expressly supplies neither a polynomial algorithm nor an NP-hardness proof for any standard fixed-k case with k≥2. The surviving results are material but incomplete, so PARTIAL is accurate and the exact target is not fully resolved.",
  "overall": "VERIFIED",
  "checks_performed": [
    "Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json as evidence inputs; used no web or other solution material.",
    "Verified SHA-256: /evidence/parent.json = ac8e93706ae8e7a430b0e804ec300545326370f2ee32584573ee72dded925651 and /evidence/source.json = 4e86dafba3ebc98f6d79e7b8ab94e032990fb429300f2c66ff29529805f3af68.",
    "Checked the exact source definition of H3, the fixed-k problem, and the stated H1/H2 polynomial boundary.",
    "Reproved each universal claim from the definitions, including all quantifier and input-model restrictions.",
    "Created and ran /work/h3_audit_exact_checker.py (SHA-256 7cb282f2125c9f4d12c2b6f95ba858df97bb93f24d0f6e5b8f63620132f656a9).",
    "Exact checker output: PASS on 20,624 construction instances, 10,288 contraction instances, 33,856 compression/minimality graphs, and all explicit sharpness and seven-vertex witnesses."
  ]
}
--- END AUDIT ---

Use native adversarial self-critique only. Do not read or use any retrieval result, external memory, treatment receipt, or database. Return revision-schema JSON. Use treatment_status PLAIN_SELF_CRITIQUE and empty receipt_path, receipt_sha256, retrieved_entry_ids, acted_on_entry_ids, and dismissed_hits.
